1.title: Question: why use a long spanner?

q.Q1: Q1. A force of 40 N is applied at the end of a spanner 0.25 m long. Calculate the moment.
q.Q2: Q2. Why are door handles placed far from the hinges?

q.Q3: Q3. A child of weight 300 N sits 2 m from the pivot of a seesaw. How far from the pivot must an adult of weight 600 N sit on the other side to balance?
q.Q4: Q4. A uniform metre rule is balanced at the 50 cm mark. A 2 N weight hangs at the 10 cm mark. Where must a 5 N weight hang to balance it?

3.title: Test: weight of the beam and reactions

q.Q5: Q5. A uniform beam 2 m long, weight 100 N, is pivoted at its centre. A 50 N load hangs 0.8 m to the left of the pivot. What force at the right end (1 m from the pivot) balances it?
q.Q6: Q6. Why does a uniform beam's weight have no moment about a pivot at its centre?

q.Q7: Q7. Two forces of 20 N act in opposite directions on opposite sides of a steering wheel of diameter 0.4 m. Calculate the torque.
q.Table: Q8. Moment of a single force or a couple?

q.Q9: Q9. A wheelbarrow carries a load of 600 N whose centre is 0.4 m from the wheel axle. The handles are 1.2 m from the axle. Calculate the upward force needed to lift it and explain why the load should be placed near the wheel.
